newsitem.title: USA: Firefighters gain upper hand on California wildfire.
newsitem.headline: Firefighters gain upper hand on California wildfire.

text.p: Firefighters on Sunday said they were gaining the upper hand on a wildfire along a scenic stretch of California coast, allowing evacuated residents to return to their homes and businesses to reopen.

Cooler temperatures, higher humidity and a drop in the winds aided fire crews battling the blaze, which broke out on Friday afternoon in a canyon near the town of Big Sur, about 150 miles (240 kms) south of San Francisco.

The fire, burning in the Ventana wilderness area of the Los Padres National Forest, an area famous for its natural beauty, stood at 650 acres (260 hectares) on Sunday, said fire information officer Larry Hornberger.

Firefighters said the blaze was 55 percent contained, an improvement over Saturday evening's 45 percent. If weather conditions remain favorable, firefighters said they would expect containment in the coming days.
"It looks like we're getting the upper hand, making some good headway," Hornberger said. "Things are really looking positive."

Firefighters lifted an evacuation order for houses and businesses along a five-mile (eight-km) stretch on the east side of Highway One, a popular route that winds along the California coast, Hornberger said.
"Things are returning to normal," he said.
The fire no longer immediately threatened about 25 homes and a half-dozen businesses, including the well-known Ventana Inn, which lies about two miles (three kms) south of Big Sur.
A 37-mile (60-km) section of Highway One that was closed on Saturday was reopened on Sunday at noon, Hornberger said.
One travel trailer was destroyed in the blaze but so far no homes have been lost and there have been no injuries.

About 1,000 firefighters were battling the blaze, backed by nine air tankers and eight helicopters. Officials estimated the cost to date of the multi-agency fire fighting effort to be nearly $533,000, but said the total could reach $1.5 million.
The cause of the fire was still unknown and was under investigation.
